title: Max grows a giant pumpkin (it exploded first)

beats.text: Max's giant pumpkin just burst open. All he did was water it.
Let's rewind to the day he planted it.
He wants one his kids can sit on. They bring the wagon.
It stays tiny: one small root clump can't feed the whole plant.
So Max buries the vine, and every leaf joint grows its own roots.
Then he waters in floods. The inside swells faster than the skin stretches. Crack.
Steady drip water keeps the skin in step, even at 20 kilos a day.
But the swelling pumpkin shoves its vine aside, and the stem cracks.
At 90 degrees to the vine, the stem rolls instead of ripping.
Underneath, a pumpkin heavier than a car sits in wet soil, rotting.
Clean sand drains fast and lets it slide, so the bottom stays dry.
Harvest day. It weighs over a tonne, the plank folds, and the wagon looks tiny.
A lifting ring spreads the weight over wide straps, so no spot takes it all.
In one piece this time, kids riding behind. Ron Wallace's 3,156-pound record rode the same way. Which disaster would have ended your pumpkin first?

cta: Which disaster would have ended your pumpkin first?
